goalInOwnWords: Build a little factory line from scrap to gold bars and make as much money as you can in 6 shifts. Ship enough bars and you get stars. The money is your score.
stoppedWhere: The results screen after my second finished game ($3690, 2 stars, 11 ingots short of 3 stars), right after sending the survey and getting the code.
stoppedWhy: I got a new personal best and I am done for now. The first 3 minutes were the fun part. In the middle of each game I am just waiting or guessing, there is nobody's score to beat and nothing I would show a friend. If a friend sent me a score to beat I would open it again.

stuck.where: Real game, shift 3 pick screen, Splitter
stuck.what: I put the Splitter on the lit belt tile like the tip said and the pay dropped to $0 in red. I could not see how to take it back: Undo, Turn and Back to the shelf were hidden under the pay line and the Start button.
stuck.gotOutHow: Scrolled the bottom panel by luck, found Undo, tapped it.

stuck.what: Why every shift paid exactly $600 whatever I picked (second hopper, tuner on the crusher, nothing). The tip under my results kept saying the crusher was the problem.
stuck.gotOutHow: Not in game 1. In game 2 I opened the Tips button (it had a dot), read that the furnace is usually the slowest thing and that a tuner makes a furnace take 2 seconds instead of 3, and put the tuner on the furnace: $888.

stuck.where: Pick screen, shifts 2 and 5, the card the foreman wants
stuck.what: My tap on the Furnace card did nothing, the card is half off the bottom of the phone screen and the tap landed below the screen. I thought the game froze for a second.
stuck.gotOutHow: Tapped the part of the card I could see.

stuck.what: The card said 'On its own: $40 more a shift' (the only green number) but the second hopper made no extra money, and the old hopper just sat there 'stuck'.
stuck.gotOutHow: Did not work it out. I stopped picking hoppers.

confused: What a Splitter does: it sends things up and down, not on to the next machine, so it broke my line and nothing said that until I read it in the Tips later.
The 'what held you back' tip said the crusher held me back and to add a Tuner next to it, and it kept saying it after I had added a Tuner next to it. The real slow machine was the furnace.
'On its own: $40 more a shift' on the Scrap Hopper card, which was not true for my line either time.
In the lesson, 'Your line needs Hopper > Crusher > Furnace > Dock' had ticks on only two and the game still said 'Line closed, start the shift'.
Only the arrows on the belt told me which side of the crusher the furnace goes on, and the game never said so.
The results screen says 'this test version has no leaderboard' and a line below says 'No connection, so no board', and those are two different reasons.
I never found out why I only get one new part a shift and cannot keep two of the three offered cards.
annoyed: Four shifts in a row of exactly $600 in the first game and nothing I could do about it.
Cards cut off at the bottom of the screen, and the card the foreman asks for is often the half-hidden one. The button list even pointed me at a spot below the screen.
Undo, Turn and Back to the shelf are hidden under the sticky 'This shift will pay' line and the Start button until you scroll.
The Start button glows orange even when the pay line says $0 or $18 in red.
No leaderboard and no share button, so my score has nobody to beat and nothing to show a friend.
A lot of small text in the bottom half of the phone. After the first lesson I stopped reading it.
The help that actually explained the machines (Tips) was hidden behind a small button and I only found it when I was already stuck.
pleased: The first lesson: three shifts, $37 then $111 then $576, all in under 3 minutes, with all three stars at the end.
Gold bars coming out of the furnace with a burst of stars and +$24 numbers, and the score counter rolling up at 4x.
4x speed stays on from one shift to the next.
The pay preview ('This shift will pay $888 (up $288)'): moving a part and watching that number was the closest thing to a game.
Foreman Sal's one-line instructions in the lesson, one thing at a time.
The results screen: 'NEW PERSONAL BEST', '+$576 over your best', '11 ingots short of three stars' and the shift-by-shift bars.
The little moving pictures inside the Tips panel once I found it.
bestMoment: Second game, shift 5: after reading in Tips that the furnace is the slow one, I put the Tuner under the furnace, the preview jumped from $600 to $888, and it was true when the shift ran.
worstMoment: First game, shifts 3 to 6: doing what the tip told me, then getting exactly $600 again and again while the same tip kept repeating.
oneChange: A board where I can see my friends' scores (or a card I can post) so a score has someone to beat.
